findings.location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 1: 'the loop ends when all_reuse is true')
findings.issue: In this slice a cell is `reuse: true` only when it has passing gate-grade evidence. Freshness alone no longer counts. Several states repeat on every run and never turn into passing evidence: a smoke-only module or specs with notes (`not-gradeable`, `scenario-notes`), a missing Firefox binary (`browser-unavailable`), a persistent install/boot failure, Docker or Playwright absent (`skipped`, nothing appended, so the cell stays `missing`), and a failing cell in headless, which patches nothing. In each case `per_version[V].rerun` keeps listing `e2e`, so the Fase 1 loop that ends on `all_reuse` never ends. The contract avoids this with `phase1_reuse` (which excludes e2e) and `e2e_step`/'E2E loop ended', but both are deferred to CAP-1, and the interim gives no replacement exit.
findings.implementation_impact: Following the docs literally loops forever: a container boots again on every iteration for a smoke-only module or a host without Firefox. In headless, any failing E2E cell never returns. Today's freshness-based `all_reuse` did end in these cases, so this is a regression the slice introduces.
findings.suggestion: Give the interim loop its own exit: end V's Fase 1 loop when every layer other than `e2e` reuses AND the E2E step has run once this session for V's in-scope cells (or its output was `skipped`), whatever the cells' reasons. Or emit an interim `phase1_reuse` (no layer other than e2e/adversarial reruns) now and gate Fase 1 on it. Add a test for the smoke-only, browser-unavailable and skipped cases.

findings.location: Design Notes > Child output in history mode / Runner interim (child `status: skipped`)
findings.issue: The only skip path the spec defines is ps-run-layer's own `docker_available()` check before spawning. A child that reports `status: skipped` (Playwright absent, or Docker gone by the time the child checks) emits `versions: {}` with no `cells` and no `browsers_available`. Under the Design Notes rules, every admitted engine is then 'missing from browsers_available', which becomes `browser-unavailable`, or has no cell, which becomes `crash`. The contract (Storage, Runner > Output) says a child skip leaves NO record and the output line is `skipped`, exit 0.
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer following the Design Notes appends fake `browser-unavailable`/`crash` inconclusive records on hosts without Playwright, prints `ran`, and exits 1. That contradicts the contract the spec calls authoritative and feeds the endless loop above.
findings.suggestion: Add to 'Child output in history mode': a parseable child result with `status: skipped` appends nothing for that child. The output line is `skipped` unless some appended record is `fail`, and the exit code is 0 per Runner > Output. Add an I/O matrix row 'Playwright absent in child'.

findings.location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 2) and docs task
findings.issue: Only the e2e `--merge-only` loses its `all_reuse` gate. Today's docs (run-phases.md Fase 2: 'Saat all_reuse true, satukan jadi kanonik') still gate the Layer 2/5 `--merge-only` on `all_reuse`. With the new semantics, `all_reuse` over all versions stays false while any E2E cell is failing, not-gradeable, browser-unavailable or narrowed out, so the canonical flashlight/scenario files are never written.
findings.implementation_impact: For smoke-only modules, narrowed runs and failing cells, the aggregate never sees canonical Layer 2/5 files. Those layers read as not run or not proven, and the report blames the wrong layers.
findings.suggestion: In Interim orchestration Fase 2, state that the Layer 2 and 5 `--merge-only` also always run, with no `all_reuse` gate (as in contract Plan > Phase 2 wrap-up), and list that change in the run-phases.md docs bullet.

findings.location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration and docs task ('On Activation step 2 browser narrowing as --cells')
findings.issue: The spec never defines how the operator's run scope filters the work. Fase 1 runs `--layer e2e --versions V`, which always covers all configured browsers of V, so browser narrowing is ignored there. Fase 2 groups ALL e2e `rerun_matrix` entries, which by design include every configured cell, including narrowed-out browsers and versions. 'Narrowing as --cells' says how to pass cells, not which ones to drop. `--versions V` also re-runs browser cells of V that already pass, so a flaky newer gate-grade `fail` can override a good older pass.
findings.implementation_impact: Narrowing to Chromium (or to one version) in On Activation has no effect: Firefox and the other versions still boot in Fase 1 and Fase 2. Fase 1 also spends boots re-proving cells that already pass.
findings.suggestion: Add one rule: the orchestrator keeps the run scope (versions × browsers from On Activation; headless: the caller's set) and, in both phases, runs `--cells` built from the e2e `rerun_matrix` entries of V (Fase 1) or of all versions (Fase 2) intersected with that scope. When the intersection is empty, it runs nothing and reports the cells left out. Use `--cells` instead of `--versions V` in Fase 1.

findings.location: I/O matrix rows 'Stopped' and 'Child exit 2'; Tasks > ps-run-layer.py
findings.issue: Both rows assume records are appended as each child exits ('records only for children that already exited', 'in-flight children finish and their records append'). Today `execute()` waits for every child and `collect()` runs only afterwards. On `--stop-job`, `JobStopped` ends ps-run-layer before `collect()`, so nothing would be appended. The spec never says that appending must move into the per-child completion path, or that the stop handler must flush the results of children that already exited.
findings.implementation_impact: A straightforward port keeps batch collection. On a stop, records of already-finished versions are lost and those versions read `missing`, so they boot again even though their evidence was produced. Neither row's test can pass.
findings.suggestion: State it outright: ps-run-layer merges and appends a child's records as soon as that child is reaped, in completion order. The stop handler appends nothing more, but records already appended stay. The exit-2 rule stops scheduling new children (submit lazily instead of submitting everything to the pool up front).

findings.location: Tasks > tests (Configured-cells test) vs I/O matrix row 'Narrowed plan'
findings.issue: The task says the Configured-cells test runs `--versions 9.1 --per-version` and 'expects the other five cells in rerun_matrix'. The matrix row for the same setup ('config 3×2, no evidence') says `rerun_matrix` lists all six cells. 'Other five' only holds if 9.1:chromium has seeded passing evidence, and the task does not say to seed it.
findings.implementation_impact: The test author either writes an assertion that contradicts the matrix row, or seeds evidence nobody specified. The two tests then pin different behavior.
findings.suggestion: Pick one: either seed passing gate-grade evidence for 9.1:chromium and expect exactly the other five cells, or drop 'other five' and expect all six (matching the matrix row).

findings.location: Design Notes > Reasons ('Current e2e_scenario_notes come from _e2e_scenario_notes(module_dir) in plan and aggregate alike')
findings.issue: The contract (Aggregate) says the aggregate's emitted `e2e_scenario_notes` field comes from the selected records only. The Design Notes sentence can be read as making the aggregate's `e2e_scenario_notes` field a module scan. The spec does not say that the scan is only the comparator for the `not-gradeable`/`scenario-notes` predicates. It also does not say what the aggregate compares against when called without `--module`.
findings.implementation_impact: The aggregate may report notes that no selected record was judged under, or the opposite. The not-gradeable predicate may also crash or behave differently when `--module` is absent.
findings.suggestion: Reword: '`_e2e_scenario_notes(module_dir)` is the CURRENT notes comparator for the not-gradeable and scenario-notes predicates. The emitted aggregate field `e2e_scenario_notes` still comes from the selected records. Without --module, every cell is `missing` and the comparator is not consulted.'

findings.location: Design Notes > Plan shape (canonical mode)
findings.issue: Canonical `layers.e2e` becomes `{<browser>: {<ver>: {...}}}`, and `rerun_matrix` stays a per-version-only output. The spec does not say how canonical mode's top-level `rerun` list decides to include `e2e`. Today's `[l for l, p in plans.items() if not p['reuse']]` would raise KeyError on the nested dict. The contract's wording ('has an e2e rerun_matrix entry') is not computable in canonical mode.
findings.implementation_impact: Canonical plan calls crash or silently drop e2e from `rerun`, depending on the implementer's patch.
findings.suggestion: Add: in canonical mode, top-level `rerun` lists `e2e` when any configured cell in `layers.e2e` has `reuse: false`. Add a canonical-mode test with one stale cell.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (Headless config copy) and I/O row 'Headless narrowed'
findings.issue: Headless is an LLM-driven flow, and no task names a producer for `<module>-psm-config.headless.<session>.json`: no script or flag, only the headless.md docs. The spec's sentence says headless 'writes the caller's versions and browsers ... into' the file. Unlike the contract, it does not say the file is a COPY OF THE RESOLVED CONFIG. The required order (mint the token, write the copy, then plan) is also left implicit.
findings.implementation_impact: The model may write a JSON file with only the two keys. That drops `psm_flashlight_tag_map`, the DB image and the timeouts, so plan, runner and aggregate fall back to script defaults: wrong image tags, all cells `stale-tag`. The 'Headless narrowed' row cannot be tested end to end because nothing scripted produces the file.
findings.suggestion: Say 'copy the resolved config JSON and overwrite only `psm_target_versions`/`psm_e2e_browsers`' and give the order explicitly. Preferably add a tiny scripted producer (e.g. a resolver flag that overrides keys and writes to a path) and test it. Otherwise restate the matrix row as an aggregate test fed a 9.1-only config.

findings.location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Quickstart TDD verdict) and docs task (e2e-quickstart.md)
findings.issue: The TDD verdict step runs one cell (`--cells 9.1:chromium`) and then the aggregate. Under this slice the aggregate's `ready` is always false there, because the other five configured cells are `missing`. It also needs `--reports-dir`/`--module` and a static file. The spec does not say which field gives the TDD verdict for that one cell.
findings.implementation_impact: The quickstart's red/green signal becomes permanently red, or the doc writer points readers at `ready`. The TDD loop is unusable as documented.
findings.suggestion: Specify the verdict field: `e2e_cells['9.1']['chromium']` (`state`, `gate_grade`, `reason`, `findings`). Give the exact aggregate command (`--reports-dir`, `--module`, `--config`, `--require e2e` if static is absent) and note that `ready=false` is expected.

findings.location: Tasks > docs (SKILL.md 'Vonis fields') and Interim orchestration commands
findings.issue: SKILL.md 'Vonis dan output' runs `ps-aggregate.py --reports-dir … --module …` without `--config`. The docs task asks only for 'Vonis fields' there. An aggregate without `--config` uses the script defaults (1.7.8,8.1,9.1 × chromium,firefox) as the configured set. The contract also requires plan, ps-run-layer and aggregate to get the same `--tag-map`/`--extra-tag-map` values. The interim commands pass none to plan or aggregate, while SKILL.md says extra tags enter only through `--extra-tag-map`.
findings.implementation_impact: A project with a different `psm_target_versions`, or with an extra tag passed to ps-run-layer, gets a verdict over the wrong cell set, or every cell `stale-tag`, even though the runs were correct.
findings.suggestion: Make the docs task require `--config <cfg>` on the SKILL.md aggregate command. Add to Interim orchestration: any `--tag-map`/`--extra-tag-map` given to ps-run-layer is passed identically to every plan call and to the aggregate.

findings.location: Tasks > docs (run-phases.md bullet)
findings.issue: The run-phases.md bullet covers only `--config` and `--session`. That file still holds the commands this slice turns into exit 2: the layer table row `ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e --per-version`, the Fase 2 command `--layer <flashlight|e2e> ... --per-version --jobs <N>`, and the merge-only step `--versions <semua> --merge-only` (e2e merge-only now takes only `--module`, `--reports-dir` and `--config`).
findings.implementation_impact: After implementation the main phase reference tells the operator to run commands the scripts reject, so every interactive run hits exit 2 at Layer 4.
findings.suggestion: Extend the run-phases.md bullet to the layer table, the Fase 1/2 E2E commands (`--versions V`/`--cells`, `--session`, no `--per-version`), and the split merge-only step (e2e report view without `--versions`; Layers 2/5 ungated).

findings.location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 2)
findings.issue: Fase 2 is a single pass: plan, one `--cells` run, merge and aggregate. Two cases are left open. First, nothing says what to do when the plan has no e2e `rerun_matrix` entries: is `--cells` with an empty value an input error, or should the run be skipped? Second, nothing says what to do when the Fase 2 E2E run produces a `fail` (go back to Fase 1 for that version, or report and stop). CAP-1 loop-back is deferred, and today's docs only say 'segarkan yang masih basi'.
findings.implementation_impact: The doc writer will improvise. They might call ps-run-layer with an empty `--cells`, which is exit 2, or silently aggregate a failing gate with no fix loop.
findings.suggestion: Add: no e2e entries in scope means skip the run. Any appended `fail` means return to Fase 1 for that version (interactive) or report and stop (headless), then repeat Fase 2.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (`ps-run-layer.py --config` for every layer) / Design Notes > Runner interim
findings.issue: ps-run-layer now reads the configured set from `--config` through the shared normalizer, and the spec says this applies 'for every layer'. It does not say whether a bad `psm_e2e_browsers` (e.g. `webkitx`) or an E2E-only version problem also exits 2 for `--layer flashlight`/`scenario`. Nor does it say whether `--session` is rejected, ignored or required on non-e2e layers.
findings.implementation_impact: One implementer blocks Layer 2/5 runs on an E2E key typo. Another lets the typo through until Layer 4. Docs that pass `--session` uniformly may hit exit 2 on Layer 2.
findings.suggestion: State that only layer `e2e` validates the configured set. Other layers just forward `--config`. `--session` on a non-e2e layer is an input error (or is ignored, whichever you pick).

findings.location: Design Notes > Record ('A record holds exactly the Fields keys plus boot_wall_clock')
findings.issue: The whitelist drops child diagnostics that today's aggregate uses. `boot_log` is appended to the inconclusive reason through `_log_tail`, and `ps_domain` and `orchestrator` are also dropped. After this slice, a boot or wait-healthy failure in a cell's history carries only `errors`, with no container log tail.
findings.implementation_impact: Infra failures in history mode lose the log tail that operators use today to tell a DB failure from an image problem. That is a silent diagnostic regression.
findings.suggestion: Either allow `boot_log` (truncated) as an extra record key next to `boot_wall_clock`, or say explicitly that it is dropped and the progress log is the only source.

findings.location: Design Notes > Normalizer input
findings.issue: The normalizer spec says 'items stripped' but does not mention case. Today's `parse_browsers` lowercases ('Chromium, FIREFOX' → chromium,firefox), and existing tests assert this. Under the new exit-2 rule, 'Chromium' is either accepted or rejected depending on the implementer. The history file name and `--cells` matching depend on the exact string.
findings.implementation_impact: Configs or caller arguments with capitalized engine names either start failing with exit 2 or produce history files and cell keys that differ in case from `psm_e2e_browsers`.
findings.suggestion: Specify: browser items are lowercased before validation (versions stay as written). Keep the existing case test, and replace the silent-drop tests with exit-2 tests.

findings.location: I/O matrix row 'Boot failure'
findings.issue: The row named 'Boot failure' actually describes an install failure ('install fails before any engine', reason `install`). There is no row for a real boot failure (bring-up, wait-healthy or wait-http fails, `install` null). For that case the contract's reason order gives `errors`, not `install`, because the install cause needs an install result whose `ok` is not true.
findings.implementation_impact: Implementers may treat `install: null` as `install.ok is not true` and stamp reason `install` on every boot failure, which mislabels infra failures as install failures.
findings.suggestion: Rename the row 'Install failure', and add a 'Boot failure (wait-healthy timeout)' row: one inconclusive record per kept engine, `install: null`, reason `errors`.

findings.location: Design Notes > Timing (`#n` suffixes) / I/O matrix row 'Timings'
findings.issue: Suffixes are assigned by order of occurrence, and the matrix row reads `wait-healthy` as the DB wait and `wait-healthy#2` as the PS wait. After the manual-mode port retry (`bring-up#2`), the DB wait repeats. The PS wait then becomes `wait-healthy#3`, so a fixed reading of `wait-healthy#2` as the PS wait is wrong.
findings.implementation_impact: Tests and readers that hard-code `wait-healthy#2` as the PS wait break or misattribute time on retried boots.
findings.suggestion: State that suffixes are purely ordinal and carry no DB/PS meaning. Make the matrix test assert only the ordinal keys and that `bring-up#2` is followed by further suffixes.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 1 'the loop ends when all_reuse is true')
findings.issue: Fase 1 can only end when all_reuse is true. Some E2E states can never become reusable in this slice: ps-run-layer prints skipped because Docker or Playwright is absent and appends nothing (the cell stays missing); psm_e2e_enabled is false; headless never passes --allow-image-pull, so a missing image gives an inconclusive 'errors' record on every run; a firefox binary is missing (browser-unavailable every run); a headless run gets an E2E fail it will never patch. The contract's exit for these cases ('E2E loop ended', and in headless 'V is clean once its loop has run its stale layers once') is in Plan > Phase 1 and E2E loop ended, which this slice does not adopt.
findings.implementation_impact: The documented Fase 1 loop never ends, or the orchestrator has to invent a stop rule. Headless callers either hang or each improvise a different one.
findings.suggestion: Add an interim stop rule to Interim orchestration: the Fase 1 loop for V also ends when E2E is disabled, when ps-run-layer prints e2e_status skipped, when the same E2E reasons repeat for V after a run with no patch in between, or in headless after V's stale layers have run once. After any of these, go on to Fase 2 and report the cells as not proven.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Boundaries > Always (Plan > Derivation predicate not-gradeable in scope) + Design Notes > Plan shape (all_reuse) + Interim orchestration
findings.issue: Take a smoke-only module (authored_assertions 0) or a module whose spec notes equal the current e2e_scenario_notes. Each cell's newest gate-grade pass gets reason not-gradeable or scenario-notes, so it is never reuse:true. per_version[V].rerun therefore always lists e2e and all_reuse is never true. The contract counts not-gradeable as passing only inside steps 4 to 7, which are deferred, so the spec has no interim rule for this.
findings.implementation_impact: On every smoke-only module, the Fase 1 loop never ends, and every Fase 2 call re-boots all cells for evidence that cannot change.
findings.suggestion: State the interim rule: for the Fase 1 loop's end condition, a cell whose plan reason is not-gradeable or scenario-notes counts as done, but it still never counts toward ready. Or have the docs end the loop when the only e2e reasons left are these two, and report them.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Tasks > docs (On Activation step 2 browser narrowing as --cells) vs Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 1 --versions V; Fase 2 runs all e2e rerun_matrix entries)
findings.issue: The operator narrows the scope at On Activation, for example to chromium only. Fase 1 runs E2E as --versions V, which drives every configured browser and ignores the narrowing. per_version[V].rerun still lists e2e while the narrowed-out firefox cell is missing. Fase 2 groups every e2e rerun_matrix entry, out-of-scope cells included, into --cells. The spec never says where the narrowing is applied in these commands, or how the loop ends while out-of-scope cells stay missing.
findings.implementation_impact: Either the narrowing is silently ignored and firefox is booted anyway, or the Fase 1 loop never ends because the narrowed-out cells can never be reused.
findings.suggestion: Define it in Interim orchestration: filter the e2e entries by the operator's scope before building --cells, in both Fase 1 (--cells V:<in-scope browsers>) and Fase 2. The Fase 1 end condition then ignores e2e entries for out-of-scope cells, and the report names those cells as not proven.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 2) + Plan shape (all_reuse now includes per-cell e2e)
findings.issue: Today's docs gate the Layer 2 and Layer 5 --merge-only on all_reuse being true. all_reuse now also needs every configured E2E cell of every version to have passing evidence. The spec takes the all_reuse gate away only from the e2e report view, and says nothing about --merge-only for Layers 2 and 5. The contract's 'always, no all_reuse gate' rule sits in Plan > Phase 2, which is not in scope.
findings.implementation_impact: When any E2E cell is unproven (for example firefox missing), the canonical flashlight and scenario files are never merged. Layers 2 and 5 then also read as not run in the aggregate.
findings.suggestion: Add to the Interim orchestration Fase 2 step: run ps-run-layer.py --merge-only for flashlight and scenario unconditionally (no all_reuse gate) before the aggregate, and update run-phases.md to match.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Tasks > docs (run-phases.md bullet)
findings.issue: The run-phases.md docs task covers only --config as a ps-run-layer flag and --session on plan calls. run-phases.md still documents the table row 'ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e --per-version', the Fase 2 command '--layer <flashlight|e2e> ... --per-version --jobs <N>', and '--merge-only --versions <semua>' for e2e. All three are now exit 2 (--per-version is rejected; --merge-only --layer e2e takes only --module, --reports-dir and --config).
findings.implementation_impact: An orchestrator that follows run-phases.md, which SKILL.md says to read before running any layer, gets exit 2 on every E2E step.
findings.suggestion: Extend the run-phases.md task: rewrite the e2e table row and the Fase 1/2 e2e commands to the Interim orchestration forms (--versions V or --cells, --session, --config, no --per-version), and make the e2e --merge-only take no --versions.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Boundaries > Always (Headless config copy)
findings.issue: The spec says headless writes psm_target_versions and psm_e2e_browsers into <module>-psm-config.headless.<session>.json. Unlike cell-contract.md ('a copy of the resolved config'), it does not say that every other resolved key is kept. Those keys include psm_flashlight_tag_map, db image, ps_domain, orchestrator, startup timeout and psm_e2e_enabled. The file it describes may hold only the two keys.
findings.implementation_impact: Plan, runner, children and aggregate lose the caller's tag map and Docker settings. Tags resolve to the defaults, so every record can read stale-tag, and boots use the wrong DB image or port.
findings.suggestion: Change the wording to: the copy is the full resolved config (<psm_reports_dir>/psm-config.json content) with only psm_target_versions and psm_e2e_browsers replaced. Add a test that a tag-map key survives the copy.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (plan / ps-run-layer / aggregate commands) + Boundaries (aggregate --tag-map/--extra-tag-map)
findings.issue: The operator uses --extra-tag-map (the SKILL.md channel for tags outside psm_flashlight_tag_map) or --tag-map in ps-run-layer's passthrough. The interim plan and aggregate commands pass only --config, so they do not forward these flags. The contract requires the orchestrator to pass the same tag values to plan, ps-run-layer and aggregate.
findings.implementation_impact: Records carry the extra tag, while plan and aggregate resolve the default tag. Every cell then reads stale-tag forever and ready never becomes true.
findings.suggestion: Add to every interim plan, ps-run-layer and aggregate command: '[--tag-map M] [--extra-tag-map E] (the same values on all three when used)', and add this to the SKILL.md and run-phases.md docs tasks.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Design Notes > Plan shape (per_version[V].layers.e2e over V in --versions)
findings.issue: The plan is called with an explicit --versions entry that is not a configured string. It may be not configured at all (9.2), or numerically equal to a configured one (9.1.0 when 9.1 is configured). ps-run-layer rejects both, but for the plan the spec defines neither per_version[V].layers.e2e, nor whether e2e is in rerun, nor whether this is exit 2.
findings.implementation_impact: The plan either emits an empty or garbage e2e entry that makes all_reuse true while there is no evidence, or crashes on a lookup by browser. A 9.1.0/9.1 mismatch reads a different history file name.
findings.suggestion: State: the plan's --versions entries must equal configured strings, else exit 2 naming the configured set (the same rule as ps-run-layer). Or: a non-configured V gets layers.e2e = {} and no e2e in rerun, with a stderr note.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Design Notes > Runner interim (child exit 2) + Boundaries ('prints the Runner > Output JSON line; exit 3/1/0/2/143')
findings.issue: One child exits 2 while in-flight siblings finish and append a fail record. Two things are unspecified: whether the exit code is 2 or 3 (the 'appended fail wins' rule), and whether the Output JSON line is printed on exit 2 and with which e2e_status. The same question applies to exit 2 input errors raised before any spawn.
findings.implementation_impact: Orchestrator and tests cannot tell an input error apart from a verdict, and a parser that expects the line may break on exit 2.
findings.suggestion: Add: 'child exit 2 → exit 2 even when an appended record is fail; the Output line is still printed with e2e_status "ran", reason "input-error after <ver>" and the appended list. Input errors before spawn print no Output line.'

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Design Notes > Timing (aggregate boots[...]) + Acceptance Criteria 1 (one key per distinct boot_id)
findings.issue: The aggregate selects a record that ps-run-layer wrote: crash, browser-unavailable, or a filled cell with no child result. Such a record has boot_id null ('null for fields no engine produced'). The spec does not say whether e2e_phase_durations[ver].boots gets a null key, skips the record, or shares the sibling engine's boot. Nor does it say whether a browser-unavailable record in a version that did boot carries that boot's boot_id and boot_phases.
findings.implementation_impact: A null or 'None' key appears in boots, two engines of one boot may count the boot twice or not at all, and AC1's per-boot_id count is ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: State: records with boot_id null add nothing to boots and add browsers[engine] only with wall_clock. A browser-unavailable record for a version whose child returned copies that version's boot_id and boot_phases from the child.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Design Notes > Aggregate ('versions[ver].reason = the reason of the first cell lacking passing evidence, in psm_e2e_browsers order')
findings.issue: Take version V with chromium missing and firefox's newest gate-grade record a fail. e2e_state is fail, but the first lacking cell in browser order is chromium, so reason is missing. The spec also does not say what versions[ver].reason is when e2e_state is pass.
findings.implementation_impact: A failing version reports reason missing. Headless callers that copy e2e_state and reason get a contradictory verdict, and the pass case is implemented as null in some places and absent in others.
findings.suggestion: Define: when e2e_state is fail, reason = fail (or the first failing cell's reason); otherwise the first lacking cell's reason in psm_e2e_browsers order; reason = null when e2e_state is pass.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Design Notes > Runner interim (exit 2 input errors for --cells)
findings.issue: The --cells value is malformed: a token without ':', an empty browser list ('9.1:'), an empty token from a trailing or doubled comma, or a browser repeated inside one cell ('9.1:chromium+chromium'). The spec lists only a repeated version and a cell outside the configured set.
findings.implementation_impact: The implementer may crash with an unpacking error, silently run fewer cells, or append two records for one cell in one run.
findings.suggestion: Add to the exit 2 list: any --cells token that does not match '<ver>:<browser>(+<browser>)*' and any empty token. Inside one cell, run the browsers through the normalizer (drop duplicates) or reject them as exit 2; say which.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Boundaries > Always (ps-run-layer --config for every layer; --session for layer e2e) + Design Notes ('ps-run-layer reads --config through its own key map: configured set, ...')
findings.issue: Two cases are left open for ps-run-layer with --layer flashlight or scenario. If its --config holds an invalid configured set (webkitx, empty list, 9.1+9.1.0), the spec does not say whether ps-run-layer runs the normalizer and exits 2 for a non-E2E layer. If --session is passed to a non-e2e layer, the spec does not say whether it is accepted, ignored or exit 2.
findings.implementation_impact: Layer 2 and 5 runs fail, or don't, on an E2E-only config error depending on how it is implemented. Tests and docs then disagree on the behavior.
findings.suggestion: State: the configured-set normalizer runs only for layer e2e (other layers just forward --config). --session with a non-e2e layer is exit 2, or is ignored; pick one and test it.

findings.location: spec-psm-e2e-cap2-cap6-cell-evidence.md: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Quickstart TDD verdict) + Tasks > docs (e2e-quickstart.md)
findings.issue: The TDD loop runs only --cells 9.1:chromium, then the aggregate with --config <cfg> (3x2 configured). ready is then always false, and the aggregate exits 2 with '--static wajib' when no <module>-static.json is in the reports dir. The spec does not say which aggregate field the author reads as RED/GREEN, or whether a static scan into the reports dir is a prerequisite.
findings.implementation_impact: The documented TDD verdict step either errors out or always reads not ready, so the author cannot see the cell turn green.
findings.suggestion: Specify that the quickstart verdict reads e2e_cells['9.1']['chromium'] (state, gate_grade, reason), not ready, and that it runs ps-static-scan.py --reports-dir ... first, or that the aggregate is called with --require e2e.

findings.location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 1 'the loop ends when all_reuse is true') + Design Notes > Plan shape (all_reuse = every per_version[V].rerun empty); ps-plan-layers.py plan_per_version
findings.issue: plan_per_version loops over every entry of LAYERS, including `adversarial`, whose per-version file `<module>-adversarial-<ver>.json` is never written: Layer 3 has no per-version form, and run-phases.md runs it once in Phase 2. So per_version[V].rerun always contains `adversarial` (tests/test-ps-plan-layers.py:356-405 confirm that the entry is always present and flagged per_version_capable False). Under the spec's definition, all_reuse can therefore never be true, and the interim Fase 1 loop never terminates. The contract avoids this with `phase1_reuse` ('no layer other than e2e and adversarial reruns'), but this slice defers phase1_reuse (CAP-1) and names nothing to replace it.
findings.implementation_impact: If implemented literally, the documented Fase 1 recipe never ends. Every iteration re-plans, sees all_reuse false and reruns layers. The implementer must invent an exit rule, either by ignoring adversarial or by emitting phase1_reuse anyway.
findings.suggestion: Either emit `phase1_reuse` now (only the contract's Phase 1 definition, no tier fields) and make the interim Fase 1 loop end on it, or define the interim end condition explicitly: per_version[V].rerun ⊆ {adversarial}, and say so in run-phases.md.

findings.location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 1 E2E as `--layer e2e --versions V` until all_reuse) vs Never (blocked-* steps, E2E loop ended deferred); cell-contract.md > Plan steps 2-3 and E2E loop ended
findings.issue: Under the new per-cell plan, an E2E cell keeps `rerun` forever whenever it cannot reach passing gate-grade: a smoke-only module (authored_assertions 0 → `not-gradeable`), a spec that carries notes (`not-gradeable`/`scenario-notes`), an infra cause that repeats (`inconclusive`, `browser-notes` for a missing binary), or a real failure the operator will not fix. The contract ends the E2E loop through blocked-not-gradeable, blocked-infra, E2E loop ended and Stop convergence, all of them deferred, and the spec names no interim substitute. Today a fresh smoke-only per-version e2e file is reused (plan_layer checks only mtime, tag and coverage), so this is a new non-termination that the slice introduces.
findings.implementation_impact: For every smoke-only module, and for every host without Firefox installed, Fase 1 reboots Docker for V on every iteration with no exit. The docs writer cannot state when to stop.
findings.suggestion: Add an interim rule: the Fase 1 E2E step for V runs at most once per source fingerprint (or ends when every cell of V has passing gate-grade evidence or a reason in {not-gradeable, scenario-notes, inconclusive, browser-notes} on the current fingerprint). Report those cells as not proven and move on. Put the rule in run-phases.md.

findings.location: Tasks > docs bullet ('SKILL.md (... Fase 1/2 e2e commands ...)', 'run-phases.md (--config as ps-run-layer flag, --session <t> on every plan call)')
findings.issue: SKILL.md holds no Fase 1/2 commands. It defers them ('Perintah persis kedua fase ...: references/run-phases.md'). The commands that break live in run-phases.md: the file-convention table row `4 e2e | ps-run-layer.py --layer e2e --per-version | ya` (now exit 2), the Fase 2 command `--layer <flashlight|e2e> ... --per-version --jobs <N>` (exit 2 for e2e), the merge-only step gated by 'Saat all_reuse true' (the e2e view is ungated), and the `all_reuse adalah gerbangnya` text. The run-phases.md bullet lists only `--config` and `--session`.
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer who follows the task list literally leaves run-phases.md telling the orchestrator to run e2e with `--per-version`, which now exits 2. SKILL.md would then gain commands it deliberately keeps out.
findings.suggestion: Move 'Fase 1/2 e2e commands per Interim orchestration' (the convention-table row, the Fase 2 e2e command with --cells, the e2e merge-only without the all_reuse gate) into the run-phases.md bullet. Keep only the paragraph-level changes in SKILL.md.

findings.location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration ('Quickstart TDD verdict: ... then the aggregate (no --tier, no --e2e)'); references/e2e-quickstart.md:82
findings.issue: Today the quickstart verdict is `ps-aggregate.py --static static.json --e2e e2e.json --versions 9.1 -o verdict.json`. Under the new aggregate, `--versions 9.1` against the default/interactive 3-version config is an input error (exit 2). Histories are read only with `--reports-dir` + `--module`, and a static file must exist (derived `<module>-static.json`, or `--static`). The spec gives none of these arguments. With config 3×2, `ready` is always false after a `--cells 9.1:chromium` run, and the spec does not say which field the TDD step reads as its verdict.
findings.implementation_impact: The doc writer must guess the aggregate invocation. The obvious edit (drop `--e2e`, keep `--versions 9.1`) exits 2, and readers chasing `ready` in the TDD loop never see it turn true.
findings.suggestion: Spell out the command: `ps-aggregate.py --reports-dir <psm_reports_dir> --module <module> --config <cfg> --static <static.json>`, without `--versions`. State that the TDD verdict is `e2e_cells['9.1']['chromium']` (state/gate_grade/reason), not `ready`.

findings.location: Design Notes > Child output in history mode ('admitted engine missing from browsers_available → browser-unavailable; any other admitted engine without a cell, or output that ... fails the shape check → crash') and Runner interim (only the docker_available pre-check is covered)
findings.issue: A child that finds Playwright absent emits `{status: 'skipped', versions: {}}` with no `browsers_available` and no `cells`, then exits 0 (ps-e2e-run.py main). Read literally, the Design Notes rule turns every admitted engine into `browser-unavailable` (missing from browsers_available) or `crash` (no cell). The contract (Storage; Runner > Output) says a child reporting `status: skipped` leaves no record and that the run prints `e2e_status: skipped` with exit 0, unless an appended record is `fail`. The spec's Runner interim restates only the ps-run-layer `docker_available()` pre-check, so the two rules contradict each other for the child-skip path.
findings.implementation_impact: A host without Playwright would write inconclusive records to every history on every run, and the next plan reads reason `inconclusive` instead of the E2E loop ending as skipped.
findings.suggestion: Add to Runner interim: a child output with `status: skipped` → no record for its cells; the output line is `skipped`, exit 0, unless an appended record is `fail` (contract Runner > Output). Evaluate the browser-unavailable/crash rules only on non-skipped output.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (ps-e2e-run.py per-engine notes) + cell-contract.md > Fields ('each cell gets only its own engine's notes') + Gate-grade (passing requires browser_notes empty); ps-e2e-run.py run_one_version probe_missed
findings.issue: When a requested engine fails the binary probe, run_one_version appends a version-level `browser_notes` entry ('engine tak dijalankan ...: firefox'). Today that note lives in one version-level list. The spec does not say where it goes per cell. Copied into the kept engine's cell (chromium), it makes chromium's otherwise clean pass non-passing gate-grade (reason `browser-notes`). ps-run-layer already writes the dropped engine its own `browser-unavailable` record, so the note does not belong in any kept cell.
findings.implementation_impact: A host with Firefox missing permanently blocks chromium's evidence too: the 9.1:chromium cell can never pass while the probe drops Firefox, even after a valid run.
findings.suggestion: State that the probe-drop note is not copied into any emitted cell; only ps-run-layer's browser-unavailable record represents it. List which notes are per engine (launch failure, BO-login) and keep the direct-run legacy version-level note unchanged.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Fields (`run_id` = RUN_ID of the version process, ps-run-layer's own when no child ran; `boot_id` = RUN_ID of the process that ran bring-up) + Runner > Child flags `--run-id` (deferred with slots); spec Acceptance Criteria 1, Design Notes > Timing
findings.issue: For a `crash` record the child did run (it may even have run bring-up), but `--run-id` is part of the deferred slot machinery, so ps-run-layer never learns the child's RUN_ID. The spec does not say what such a record holds for `run_id` (ps-run-layer's own? null?) or for `boot_id` (null?). The aggregate's `e2e_phase_durations[ver].boots` is keyed by boot_id, and AC1 counts 'one key per distinct boot_id of the selected records', but neither defines how a null boot_id is handled.
findings.implementation_impact: Implementers will differ on null-keyed or 'None'-keyed boots entries, or invent a synthetic id. Tests over crash/browser-unavailable records become implementation-specific.
findings.suggestion: State that records ps-run-layer writes without a child result have `run_id` = ps-run-layer's RUN_ID and `boot_id` = null, `boot_phases` = null, `boot_wall_clock` = null, and that the aggregate skips null boot_ids in `boots` (or define the key).

findings.location: Design Notes > Aggregate ('versions[ver].reason = the reason of the first cell lacking passing evidence, in psm_e2e_browsers order') vs cell-contract.md > Aggregate (e2e_state `fail` when some cell's newest gate-grade record is fail; `stale-fail`)
findings.issue: With chromium `missing` and firefox `fail`, e2e_state is `fail` but versions[ver].reason is `missing`. The reason contradicts the state. The spec also leaves open (a) the reason when e2e_state is `pass` (null?), (b) the `reason` of an e2e_cells entry whose cell has passing evidence, and (c) whether `stale-fail` replaces stale-source/stale-tag in e2e_cells too or only in the per-version reason (the contract places it in the per-version sentence; AC2 requires e2e_cells to carry 'a contract reason').
findings.implementation_impact: Headless callers and the Vonis summary will report 'missing' for a version that actually fails. Tests on reasons will encode whichever reading the implementer picks.
findings.suggestion: Define: when e2e_state is `fail`, reason = `fail` (or the failing cell's reason); when `pass`, reason = null; e2e_cells.reason = null for a cell with passing evidence; and say whether `stale-fail` applies in e2e_cells.

findings.location: Design Notes > Aggregate ('A cell with no valid record: e2e_cells entry {state: null, ..., reason: "missing"}'; 'corrupt-history overrides the selected record's reason') vs cell-contract.md > Plan reasons (corrupt-history before missing) and Storage
findings.issue: In a history whose only lines are corrupt, the cell has no valid record, so the Design Notes rule gives it reason `missing`, and the corrupt-history override has no selected record to apply to. The plan's reason order puts `corrupt-history` first ('while no valid line follows the last corrupt line'), so the plan says `corrupt-history` for the same cell. 'Reasons as in the plan' then breaks.
findings.implementation_impact: Plan and aggregate disagree on the same cell. A test of the I/O 'Corrupt line' row with a corrupt-only file gets different answers depending on which script it targets.
findings.suggestion: Add: a cell with no valid record whose file ends in a corrupt line gets reason `corrupt-history` (state null, gate_grade false); `missing` only when the file is absent or has no lines.

findings.location: Acceptance Criteria 2 ('Given any configured cell whose newest gate-grade record is not passing, or with no gate-grade record, when aggregating, then ready=false ...')
findings.issue: The criterion fixes neither `--require` nor the other layer inputs. The aggregate's default `--require` is every layer, so ready=false holds trivially from missing flashlight/adversarial files whatever the E2E evidence. The criterion therefore cannot detect a broken E2E gate. AC1 does pin `--require static,e2e` and a conclusive static file.
findings.implementation_impact: A test written to AC2 passes even if the E2E per-cell gate is missing.
findings.suggestion: Rewrite AC2 with the same setup as AC1 (config 3×2, conclusive static for the three versions, `--require static,e2e`, five cells passing). The sixth cell is not passing / has no gate-grade record → ready=false and e2e_cells names that cell with its reason.

findings.location: Tasks > docs ('On Activation step 2 browser narrowing as --cells') vs Design Notes > Interim orchestration (Fase 2: 'one plan call over all configured versions ... group its e2e rerun_matrix entries by version into one --cells call')
findings.issue: rerun_matrix always lists every configured cell, so the Fase 2 recipe drives all of them. Nothing says how the operator's narrowing (browsers, and also versions, which today SKILL.md applies 'seragam di semua lapis') filters that grouping. It is also unclear which versions Fase 1 loops over when versions are narrowed, and whether the docs must warn that narrowing now always leaves ready=false. The contract handles scope through `e2e_next_cells` filtering and `blocked-by-scope`, both deferred.
findings.implementation_impact: The doc writer must invent the filter step, or the interactive run ignores the operator's scope and boots all six cells in Fase 2.
findings.suggestion: State the interim rule: Fase 1 loops only over the scoped versions; Fase 2 keeps only rerun_matrix e2e entries inside scoped versions × scoped browsers before grouping into --cells. On Activation must tell the operator that cells left out stay unproven and ready stays false.

findings.location: Design Notes > Interim orchestration (aggregate command `ps-aggregate.py --reports-dir … --module … --config …`) vs cell-contract.md > Config keys > Image tag ('the orchestrator passes the same values to plan, ps-run-layer and aggregate')
findings.issue: SKILL.md's Validate section lets the operator add tags with `--extra-tag-map` (and `--tag-map`). Plan already takes them, and ps-run-layer takes them from passthrough, but the interim aggregate command and the docs task omit them for the aggregate. The aggregate would then resolve a different tag than the runner stamped, so every cell reads stale-tag.
findings.implementation_impact: Any run with an extra tag gives ready=false with reason stale-tag on every cell, and nothing in the docs explains why.
findings.suggestion: Add to the docs task and the interim commands: forward the same `--tag-map`/`--extra-tag-map` to plan, `ps-run-layer.py` (after `--`) and `ps-aggregate.py`.

findings.location: Design Notes > Runner interim (child exit 2: 'in-flight children finish and their records append'; Stop: 'append only records of children that already exited with a result'); ps-run-layer.py execute()/collect()/_run()
findings.issue: Today execute() submits every child to a ThreadPoolExecutor at once and collect() runs only after all children finish. JobStopped (raised on the main thread by fl._on_sigterm) aborts main() and _run() returns 143, so nothing is ever merged. The spec states the outcomes but not the mechanism: whether records are appended as each child completes or in one batch at the end, and how 'no further queued child starts' coexists with submit-all. The stop outcome depends on that timing.
findings.implementation_impact: A batch-at-end implementation appends nothing on stop (violating 'records for children that already exited'). A submit-all executor cannot stop queued children on an exit 2. Either way the I/O rows 'Child exit 2' and 'Stopped' fail.
findings.suggestion: State that in history mode ps-run-layer schedules children itself (start a child only while no child has exited 2), appends each child's records as soon as that child is reaped, and catches JobStopped in main to skip unreaped children before returning 143.

findings.location: Design Notes > Child output in history mode ('output that does not parse or fails the shape check → crash')
findings.issue: 'The shape check' is undefined. validate_layer_shape and collect()'s stray-version rejection (exit 2 today) belonged to the legacy merge. The spec does not say which keys a child payload and each `cells.<engine>` entry must carry, whether a payload that reports a version other than the requested one is `crash` or exit 2, or whether a cell missing a Fields key counts as a shape failure or is stored and later read as `incomplete-record`.
findings.implementation_impact: The boundary between `crash`, `incomplete-record` and exit 2 is decided ad hoc, and tests for malformed child output cannot be written from the spec.
findings.suggestion: Define the minimal shape: top-level dict with `versions[<requested ver>]` holding `cells` (a dict of dicts), `boot_phases`, `boot_id`, `run_id`, `image_tag`. A stray version → crash for the admitted cells (not exit 2). Missing per-cell Fields are stored as null and left to the incomplete-record rule.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (aggregate --config, versions replace --versions/static versions) vs Tasks > tests ('rewrite e2e-file tests against histories')
findings.issue: Many existing non-E2E aggregate CLI tests call `--static s.json --versions 8.1` without `--config` (tests/test-ps-aggregate.py around 391, 427, 611, 786, 812). They also assert the 'static with zero versions → exit 2 nol versi' gate (line 745-752) and the unscanned exit 2 (13d). With configured versions defaulting to 1.7.8,8.1,9.1, `--versions 8.1` becomes exit 2 (differs), an empty static no longer exits 2, and the unscanned gate is removed. The tests task covers only the E2E-file tests.
findings.implementation_impact: After the change, the static/flashlight/adversarial test suites fail en masse, and the implementer must decide alone how to rewrite or invert them, including which old honesty guards still need a replacement test.
findings.suggestion: Add to the tests task: give every aggregate CLI test a config whose psm_target_versions matches its static payload; replace the 'nol versi' and unscanned exit-2 tests with 'version missing from static → layer not conclusive, ready=false, exit not 2'; keep a test that an empty configured list exits 2.

findings.location: Design Notes > Normalizer input ('items stripped') and Runner interim (`--cells` parsing); tests/test-ps-e2e-run.py:243
findings.issue: Case handling is unspecified. parse_browsers lowercases today ('Chromium, FIREFOX' → chromium,firefox), and an existing test expects that. The normalizer contract lists the allowed engines in lowercase and says only 'items stripped'. Also unspecified: a browser repeated inside one --cells version (`9.1:chromium+chromium`), an empty segment (`9.1:`), and a token without a colon.
findings.implementation_impact: A config 'Chromium' either works or exits 2 depending on the implementer. The existing parse_browsers test must be kept, rewritten or dropped without guidance.
findings.suggestion: State whether engines are lowercased before validation (recommended, to keep current behaviour), and that a repeated browser within a --cells version, an empty browser list, or a malformed token are exit 2.

findings.location: Boundaries > Always (`--versions` in plan stays run scope; e2e covers configured cells) ; ps-plan-layers.py --per-version
findings.issue: Plan `--versions` may name a version outside the configured set (for example `9.1.0` against configured `9.1`, or `9.2` passed explicitly). The runner rejects such a cell (exit 2). For the plan, the spec does not say what per_version[V].layers.e2e holds, or whether `e2e` appears in per_version[V].rerun, for a non-configured V. With no configured cells for V, a natural implementation emits an empty e2e map and silently reports E2E as reusable for V.
findings.implementation_impact: Fase 1 on a mistyped version reports E2E clean and never runs it.
findings.suggestion: Make a plan `--versions` entry that is not exactly a configured string an input error (exit 2), mirroring the runner, or define per_version[V].layers.e2e for it.

findings.location: Boundaries > Never ('Readers must still classify warm/partial/not-run records correctly') vs Tasks > tests
findings.issue: This done-criterion has no test in the tests task. The reasons `warm-only`, `partial` and `not-run`, `not_run_cells`, and gate-grade exclusion for `boot: warm`/`scenario_set: partial` can only be exercised with hand-written records, since this slice never produces them.
findings.implementation_impact: Reader paths for records written by later slices ship untested, and a regression there goes unnoticed until CAP-3/4/5 land.
findings.suggestion: Add a tests bullet: hand-written warm, partial and not-run records give plan reasons warm-only/partial/not-run, are never gate-grade, never hide an older gate-grade record, and a newest not-run record appears in the aggregate's not_run_cells.

findings.location: Design Notes > Reasons ('Current e2e_scenario_notes come from _e2e_scenario_notes(module_dir) in plan and aggregate alike') vs cell-contract.md > Aggregate (e2e_scenario_notes 'comes from the selected records only')
findings.issue: The spec does not say whether the aggregate's output field `e2e_scenario_notes` is the live, git-derived notes from _e2e_scenario_notes or the notes of the selected records (contract). The Design Notes sentence reads as if it governs the field. It can also be read as covering only the 'current' value used for the not-gradeable/scenario-notes comparison.
findings.implementation_impact: After a spec is fixed but before re-proving, the two readings give different report output. Tests on e2e_scenario_notes are ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: Say explicitly: the live notes are used only for the not-gradeable/scenario-notes comparison, and the emitted `e2e_scenario_notes` field is the union of the selected records' scenario_notes (contract), or state the deviation.

findings.location: Design Notes > Runner interim (exit-2 input-error list; 'ps-run-layer reads --config through its own key map ... configured set, psm_flashlight_tag_map, psm_flashlight_startup_timeout')
findings.issue: The contract scopes these rules 'for layer e2e', but the spec lists them unscoped: psm_reports_dir equal to the module root, a --screenshot-dir inside the module, and normalizer validation of the configured set. It is unclear whether `--layer flashlight|scenario` runs (which now also get `--config`) must exit 2 on a bad psm_e2e_browsers or a reports dir equal to the module root. psm_flashlight_startup_timeout has no consumer in this slice (it bounds the deferred no-slots wait), and the spec does not say whether to read and validate it.
findings.implementation_impact: A config typo in psm_e2e_browsers could start breaking Layer 2/5 runs, or be ignored, depending on the implementer. Dead config reads invite drift.
findings.suggestion: Scope the configured-set read and the reports-dir/screenshot-dir checks to `--layer e2e` (including e2e --merge-only for the configured set). Drop psm_flashlight_startup_timeout from this slice's key map, or name its use.

findings.location: I/O matrix row 'Headless narrowed' ('headless copy holds psm_target_versions = 9.1')
findings.issue: The headless flow is prose the model follows (references/headless.md). No script writes the copy, and no task adds one. The first half of the row (the copy's content) therefore cannot be tested with the Verification commands. The spec also does not say whether the copy writes the values as a comma-separated string or a list (the normalizer accepts both), or that every other key of psm-config.json is copied unchanged (tag map etc.).
findings.implementation_impact: The row cannot be verified. Different doc wordings will yield copies that differ in format or drop keys such as psm_flashlight_tag_map, and that makes cells read stale-tag.
findings.suggestion: Mark the copy half as doc-only and test only the aggregate/plan half (a config whose psm_target_versions is '9.1'). State in the headless.md task: copy psm-config.json verbatim and overwrite only psm_target_versions/psm_e2e_browsers with comma-separated strings.

findings.location: Tasks > tests ('the Configured-cells test runs as --versions 9.1 --per-version (no plan --browsers) and expects the other five cells in rerun_matrix') vs I/O row 'Narrowed plan' ('lists all six cells')
findings.issue: Without plan --browsers there is no 'one' cell for the other five to be relative to. With no evidence all six cells are listed, which matches the I/O row. 'The other five' is a leftover of the contract test that used `--browsers chromium`.
findings.implementation_impact: An implementer may seed 9.1:chromium with passing evidence to make 'five' true, or assert five entries and fail against the I/O row.
findings.suggestion: Reword: 'expects all six configured cells in rerun_matrix (or, with 9.1:chromium seeded passing, the other five)'.

findings.location: cell-contract.md > Storage (corrupt when 'started_at is not UTC ISO-8601') + Fields ('UTC ISO-8601 with microseconds')
findings.issue: The accepted textual form is not pinned: `+00:00` versus `Z`, and microseconds required or optional. On the project's minimum Python (requires-python >=3.10), datetime.fromisoformat rejects the `Z` suffix, so a reader built on it marks `Z` lines as corrupt. If the writer and reader pick different forms, every line becomes corrupt and the cell reads corrupt-history.
findings.implementation_impact: There is a silent risk of every record being read as corrupt across implementations or hand-written test fixtures.
findings.suggestion: Pin the writer format (`datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(timespec='microseconds')`, i.e. `+00:00`). State that readers accept an offset of zero, with or without fractional seconds, and also `Z`.

findings.location: Tasks > docs ('README --config on ps-run-layer', 'ps-run-layer.py docstring example'); docs/psm/README.md; ps-run-layer.py module docstring
findings.issue: docs/psm/README.md has no ps-run-layer command, only prose mentions at lines 84, 89, 355 and 369, so it is unclear where '--config on ps-run-layer' goes. The ps-run-layer docstring describes exit codes as 2/1/0 and the canonical-file merge as the script's purpose.
